title: Round 6 / ECDLP-17: blind adversarial review of Theorems A, A' and B
question: Are the restricted-model lower bounds HYP-5a550ab6 (Theorems A, A') and HYP-eda6732a (Theorem B) correct as stated, with correct hypotheses, and are they already known (Lange–Winterhof, Satoh, Shparlinski et al.)?

claims:
Theorem A is correct with corrected hypotheses: the bounds (N-1)/2 (pole degree) and (N-1)/6 (polynomial total degree) hold for all r, p>3, 2<=N<=r-1; the proof step 'h=0 implies r=0 in F_p' is incomplete (p | r with r != p occurs: p=5, r=10, y^2=x^3+3x, P=(2,2)); repair: h=0 makes the pole set

-invariant so deg >= r. Hypothesis r != p is unnecessary.

Theorem A' is correct (SLP regular at every kP, constants arbitrary, no comparisons): length >= log2((N-1)/6), so the stated log2((N-1)/12) is valid but not sharp; the Omega(n^2) bit-cost conclusion holds only under the assumed per-operation charge Omega(log q) and is not a bit-complexity bound for ECDLP.

Theorem B is correct as stated; r prime can be weakened to r odd, r>=5 (p>3). Proof: H(Q)=F(Q+P)+F(Q-P)-2F(Q)-2 is even, has r-5 distinct zeros +-kP (2<=k<=(r-3)/2) and pole divisor of degree exactly 6 deg g.

Counterexample search (208 Theorem-B cases, 138 Theorem-A rows, p<=61) found no violation; rational interpolants with pole degree (N+1)/2 exist, so the constant 1/2 in A is essentially attained for rational f; the author's conjecture m*=r is false for rational f.

Novelty: not established; Lange-Winterhof (COCOON 2002), Satoh (WCC 2005), Kiltz-Winterhof (2006) concern ECDL interpolation lower bounds but their theorem statements were not accessible, so overlap is likely for the polynomial parts of A and B.
next_action: PI: correct HYP-5a550ab6 statement/proof (drop r != p, use pole-orbit argument; A' constant 6 and model hypotheses; Theorem B r odd); obtain full texts of Lange-Winterhof 2002, Satoh 2005, Kiltz-Winterhof 2006 to settle novelty; then register REV and consider Lean formalization of Theorem B.
